courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: A Systems Approach to Health Promotion Across Diverse Populations
courses.description: Analyze the impact of social, cultural, and ecological factors on health decision-making, healthcare delivery, and health promotion behaviors among diverse populations and settings through application of theory, ethical principles, and health promotion methodologies. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted: Nursing 395H, 395 (Topic 7), Nurse Professional 395D. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395G, 395O, and 395Q.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395G, 395O, and 395Q.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Health Policy for Diverse Systems and Populations
courses.description: Discuss the expanded role of clinical leaders in health policy advocacy at the organizational, community, state, national, and international level through examination of socio-political and economic contexts of health, advocacy, policy development, analysis, implementation, and evaluation. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted: Nursing 395J, 395 (Topic 8), Nurse Professional 395E. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Health Care Economics and Finance
courses.description: Explore basic economic theory, market drivers and restraints, health care budgets, financial management and reimbursement in systems, cost/benefit analysis of programs or initiatives, and health care, entrepreneurism through theory, application, and clinical leadership principles. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Only one of the following may be counted: Nursing 395P, 395 (Topic 9), Nurse Professional 395F. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Translating Evidence into Nursing Practice
courses.description: Appraise literature critically and make recommendations for evidence-based practice changes, innovations, or guidelines to improve health care outcomes. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395G and Nurse Professional 395G may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Leadership in Organizations and Systems
courses.description: Explore leadership and systems theories, including philosophies, cultures, structures, processes, information management, interprofessional communication, and other areas relevant to healthcare organizations. Examine the role of the Doctor of Nursing Practice nurse within the larger context of the health care system. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395K and Nurse Professional 395K may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Quality Improvement and Safety Principles and Methods
courses.description: Apply the science of quality improvement and implementation to improve organizational effectiveness and health outcomes. Discuss strategies to enhance complex system thinking, process analysis, and measuring and monitoring quality and safety indicators. Explore developing and evaluating cost-effective improvement initiatives and implementation of evidence-based practices. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395L and Nurse Professional 395L may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Epidemiology and Population Health
courses.description: Explore the activities of international, national, state, and local entities in relation to population health, health disparities, and the needs of priority populations. Discuss basic epidemiological principles, disaster and emergency prevention and response, and inter-professional collaboration to identify, analyze, and evaluate key population health issues. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395M and Nurse Professional 395M may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Roles and Theory Foundations of the Nursing Practice Leadership Role
courses.description: Engage in both practicum experiences and self-directed scholarship to explore the development of the Doctor of Nursing Practice role and its unique contributions of clinical leadership within an interdisciplinary and dynamic healthcare environment. Refine and state the tenets of their personalized conceptual or theoretical framework derived from nursing theories and related sciences with the goal of improving healthcare practice outcomes and disseminating findings as a DNP clinical leader. Identify a clinical area of interest and begin to demonstrate standards of DNP practice, to improve healthcare outcomes for diverse populations. Two lecture hours and four laboratory hours a week for a semester. Only one of the following may be counted: Nursing 395E, 395O, Nurse Professional 395O. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Research and Evaluation Methods I
courses.description: Examine basic concepts in research and evaluation methods including quantitative and qualitative designs, descriptive and inferential statistics, reliability and validity, and data collection and extraction strategies that DNPs use to evaluate evidence-based literature. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395 (Topic 5) and Nurse Professional 395Q may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and consent of instructor.
courses.offering: Offered on the letter-grade basis only.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Research and Evaluation Methods II
courses.description: Apply research design, statistical and qualitative techniques, and data collection/extraction methods to the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Scholarly Project and other research, quality assurance, and program evaluation activities. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395 (Topic 6) and Nurse Professional 395R may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395Q.
courses.prereqText: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395Q.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Healthcare Information Systems
courses.description: Discuss interprofessional approaches to informatics by incorporating health specific disciplines (such as nursing and pharmacy), computer science, and information science. Examine resources and methods required to apply informatics and technology to implement clinical guidelines, support communication systems, and enhance safe health care delivery. Explore opportunities to analyze information requirements, design system alternatives, and consider the management of resources. Three lecture hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395S and Nurse Professional 395S may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing; Nurse Professional 395G, 395O and 395Q or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NRP
courses.title: Clinical Leadership Specialization Seminar and Practicum III
courses.description: Utilize practicum experiences and self-directed scholarship to implement a significant pilot study, a program evaluation project, a quality improvement project, a policy analysis, or a practice-change initiative in an identified area of clinical leadership specialization. Discuss implementation strategies, including incorporation of the most recent evidence-based practice in the management of patient care within an interdisciplinary practice model and utilization of evidence-based research in the clinical management of individuals, families, and communities. Explore leadership and systems analysis in complex organizations, managing interdisciplinary teams, improving educational systems, and developing and implementing quality improvement projects and evidence-based management systems to improve patient, population, and health systems outcomes. For 395V, one lecture hour and eight laboratory hours a week for one semester; for 495V, one lecture hour and twelve laboratory hours a week for one semester; for 595V, one lecture hour and sixteen laboratory hours a week for one semester. Nursing 395V and Nurse Professional 395V may not both be counted. Offered on the letter-grade basis only. Prerequisite: Graduate standing and Nurse Professional 395U, 495U, or 595U.
